verdicts.proposal_name: P1: Procyclical credit supply zeta(x) + tau/kappa_b recalibration
verdicts.critique: I measured the proposal's own key object off the shipped solution files and it fails on its central claim. (1) THE V IS STRUCTURALLY ONE-SIDED. b_refin_0.csv / b_refin_I.csv take exactly three values {0.2105, 0.2632, 0.3158} and 0.3158 is the maximum. panel_functions_gs21.py:117-119 gives b[t+1] = (eta=0)*((1-invest)*b + invest*b/g) + (eta=1)*b_refin, so b can only (a) stay, (b) be DIVIDED by g=1.14, or (c) jump to a b_refin value <= 0.3158. Therefore b_it <= max(b*) ALWAYS. The realized support lies entirely on the left arm of the alleged V. The envelope-theorem symmetry argument is inapplicable to this model as written, and no tau/kappa_b recalibration changes it, because raising tau just moves b* up and the support up with it. (2) G IS NOT AN ENVELOPE GAIN AND IS NOT ZERO AT THE VERTEX. GS21.m:250-256/286 computes P0_up = max_b' [pi + (1-kappa_b)Q_0(b') - Q_0(b) + EP0(b')], i.e. refinancing is MANDATORY when eta=1 (b'=b is available but still pays kappa_b*Q_0(b)). So G(b*) = -kappa_b*Q_0(b*) < 0. Measured on the grid at mid (z,x): G/P_down = +0.00826, +0.00651, +0.00458, +0.00251, +0.00045, -0.00126, -0.00197 at b = 0, 0.053, 0.105, 0.158, 0.211, 0.263, 0.316. MONOTONE DECREASING across the entire realized support, and the -0.00197 at b* matches -kappa_b*Q_0/P = -0.00197 to five decimals. (3) THE LINEARITY MEASUREMENT. Sampling 40 synthetic cross-sections (N=1000, common x ~ N(0, 0.05704), z ~ N(0, 0.05389), b on the realized support {0, .2105, .2632, .3158} and /g), R^2 of G/P on the CURRENT raw chars {size, bm, mkt_lev} = 0.898; adding book_lev = 0.996. FM regresses on RAW levels (fama_functions.py:152-165, standardization commented out), so FM spans 90-99.6% of this channel exactly. Meanwhile the rank-standardized bases DKKM must use give R^2 = 0.548 (rank-linear) and 0.801 (rank + full quadratic). DKKM's basis represents the proposed object WORSE than FM's does. (4) RAISING kappa_b MAKES IT MORE LINEAR, NOT LESS. G(kappa_b) ~ G(0.004) - (kappa_b-0.004)*Q_0, and Q_0 is monotone increasing in b, so the always-paid rollover cost is a monotone-in-leverage term that scales 5x. Measured at kappa_b = 0.02: sd(G/P) does rise 0.00284 -> 0.00516, but R^2 on {size,bm,mkt_lev} RISES 0.898 -> 0.947 and with book_lev 0.996 -> 0.997. The proposal's own amplitude lever works directly against its own mechanism.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM captures it almost entirely, and the arithmetic is second-order even before that. Duration-corrected magnitude: a permanent-equivalent zeta shift is capitalized over 1/(1-rho_x*beta) = 1/(1-0.983*0.994) = 43 months, so the refinancing-option share of P is ~zeta*duration*(G/P) = 0.01*43*sd(G/P) = 0.0012 in cross-sectional sd; times the persistence-weighted theta effect (~0.4) gives a credit-beta sd of ~4.9e-4, times lambda_x = gamma_x = 0.5 gives sd(new premium) = 2.5e-4 against the measured sd(mu) = 4.0-5.6e-4. So the channel is ~25-35% of var(mu) at BEST (the proposal claims 86%, using theta*(G/P) with the zeta*duration factor silently set to 1 -- that is a 2.3x overstatement). Of that 25-35%, only 1-10% is outside FM's raw-linear span. Net incremental unspanned share of SR^2: 2.3% with the current chars, 0.1% if proposal 2 ships book_lev. Translating through the diagnosis's own span numbers (f_lin = 0.871, f_RFF360 = 0.988 of max SR^2, DKKM/FM Sharpe = sqrt(.988/.871... actually /f_FM=.932) = 1.030): f_lin falls to ~0.85 and DKKM/FM goes 1.030 -> ~1.04. To reach 3x you need f_lin = 0.110. This proposal moves you 2% of the way. FF's 2x3 sort does lose the V arm above b*, but since there IS no support above b*, FF's high-minus-low mkt_lev sort is a clean monotone spread and captures it too, modulo value-weighting. Finally the metric: Sharpe_t = SR*_t * cos_Sigma(w, w*) and SR* is bounded by the model's own HJ bound sqrt(exp(gamma_x^2)-1) = 0.533/month (GS21.m:28,138). zeta(x) adds no new shock, so max_sr cannot rise; the entire claimed gain must come from degrading FM's cosine, and I measured that degradation at ~1%.
verdicts.salvage: The only version that survives is one that first creates a two-sided leverage distribution. That requires a mechanism that pushes b ABOVE the current target: (i) capital depreciation or disinvestment in the k law of motion (panel_functions_gs21.py:119 currently has k monotone non-decreasing), so that b = coupon/capital drifts UP when the firm shrinks; or (ii) a persistent state-dependent b*(x) with enough amplitude that a firm refinanced in a boom is materially over-levered in a bust -- note b_refin currently spans only {0.2105, 0.2632, 0.3158}, i.e. two grid steps on a 20-point bgrid, so the target barely moves. Then verify BEFORE running the pipeline that (a) the realized b distribution straddles the argmin of G, and (b) R^2(G/P | raw {size, bm, mkt_lev, book_lev}) is below ~0.5. On the shipped solution it is 0.996. Separately, note GS21.m:35 sets xi = 0.03/3*3 = 0.03 while config.py:296 sets GS21_ZETA = 0.03/3 = 0.01 -- the panel is simulated at one third of the refinancing intensity the value function was solved with. Fix that before touching zeta at all; it is a 3x error in exactly the parameter this proposal wants to make stochastic.

verdicts.proposal_name: P2: Repair mkt_lev and add book_lev, distance-to-default, rolling investment rate, rolling cash-flow volatility
verdicts.critique: The mkt_lev bug is real (panel_functions_gs21.py:278, mkt_lev = book_lev * bm = b/P_ex, and b is a monthly coupon per unit capital) and worth fixing. Everything else in this proposal is neutral-to-harmful for a DKKM advantage, and one item actively destroys proposals 1 and 6. (1) ADDING book_lev KILLS P1/P6. I measured R^2 of the credit-option loading G/P on raw chars: 0.898 without book_lev, 0.996 with it. book_lev = b is exactly the linear regressor that hands FM the entire object P1 and P6 claim FM is blind to. These proposals are substitutes, not complements, and the proposal states the opposite. (2) dd IS DEAD AND WORSE THAN DEAD. I read z_cut_down.csv and z_cut_up.csv: each contains exactly ONE unique value, -0.146826, equal to zgrid.min(), at all 400 (x,b) points. So dd = (z - const)/sd is an exact affine transform of the CURRENT latent productivity state z. Since roe is a monotone transform of LAGGED z (op_cashflow_{t-1}/book_{t-1} with x cross-sectionally constant), dd is not a duplicate of roe -- it is strictly worse: it hands every method the current latent state with literally zero measurement error. The diagnosis already established that GS21's chars invert (k,b,z) exactly and that this is precisely why an MLP recovers 98.3% of the true SDF weight and why the model sits in DKKM's APT regime. dd pushes GS21 further in the wrong direction. (3) ivest REPRODUCES THE BGN agr PATHOLOGY. I computed i_cut_down mean = 39.6 against imax = 2000, so P(invest) = 1.98%/month and a 12-month rolling mean is Binomial(12, 0.0198) with P(0) = 78.7%. That is 79% exact ties, which dkkm_functions.rank_standardize (line 57, np.argsort) breaks into a persistent pseudo-random column. The BGN audit measured exactly this: feature PCs needed for 99% of variance rose from 59 to 95 when the tie-ridden agr was included. A noise char enters ONE of FM's regressors additively but ALL 3600 RFF features multiplicatively. ivest is DKKM-negative. (4) cfvol IS A PURE NOISE COLUMN ABSENT PROPOSAL 4. With a single homogeneous sigma_z, a 36-month rolling sd of roe estimates a constant; its cross-sectional variation is 100% sampling noise. Same asymmetric damage as (3).
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM benefits strictly more than DKKM. FM gets four clean extra linear regressors (K = 7 -> 11), one of which (book_lev) is the exact sufficient statistic for the only nonlinear object anyone has proposed, and one of which (dd) is the latent state itself. DKKM gets the same four inputs but must find them inside a 3600-feature ridge whose effective rank the audit measured at 20.7 (rising to only ~38 at L=10), while two of the four (ivest, cfvol) are noise that contaminates every feature multiplicatively. The proposal's own claimed benefit -- effective rank 20.7 -> 38.5 -- is worth 'maybe +1-2% of Sharpe by itself', which is the correct order and is smaller than the FM gain from four extra regressors. The measurement-error argument for cfvol is the one theoretically right idea here, but it is applied to a variable that measures nothing, so it delivers noise without signal. Net expected effect on the DKKM/FM ratio: negative or zero.
verdicts.salvage: Ship only the mkt_lev repair (it is a genuine definitional bug: use Q_0/(Q_0+P_ex) with the Q_0 interpolator already imported via panel_functions_gs21.py:15). Drop dd and ivest entirely. Replace cfvol with the thing the AIPT theory actually requires and that GS21 conspicuously lacks: independent measurement error and a reporting lag on the EXISTING chars. Concretely, report bm, roe and book_lev with i.i.d. multiplicative noise of 10-20% and a 1-3 month publication lag. That is a ~5-line change in create_panel, needs no re-solve, and is the single cheapest change that breaks the exact char->state invertibility (bm = 1/P_ex is currently exact to np.allclose) and therefore makes the optimal weight a nonlinear shrinkage map rather than a linear inversion. It is also the only change in this entire list that is asymmetrically DKKM-favourable on theoretical grounds rather than by construction, because ridge over a rich basis is exactly the right estimator for a noisy-proxy problem while unpenalized OLS on 7 factors (config.ALPHA_LST_FAMA = [0]) is exactly the wrong one.

verdicts.proposal_name: P3: Restore sigma_z to the paper value, raise rho_z to 0.985, repair the solve-vs-simulation parameter mismatches
verdicts.critique: Split this into two proposals, because one half is mandatory and the other half is counterproductive. THE HYGIENE HALF IS MANDATORY AND THE PROPOSER UNDERCOUNTED THE MISMATCHES. I verified: (a) sigma_z -- GS21.m:25 uses 0.16*sqrt((1-0.9^(2/3))/(1-0.9^2)); config.py:289 uses 0.1*0.16*sqrt((1-0.9^(3/2))/(1-0.9^2)) = 0.014034; the shipped zgrid.max() = 0.146826 equals exactly 4*0.009560/sqrt(1-rho_z^2) where 0.009560 = 0.1*0.16*sqrt((1-0.9^(2/3))/(1-0.9^2)). So the solve used the 0.1 factor AND the 2/3 exponent, and the simulation runs 1.468x wider. (b) sigma_x -- xgrid.max() = 0.153723 = 4*0.0070688/sqrt(1-rho_x^2), the 2/3-exponent value; config simulates 0.010458, 1.484x wider. (c) r -- GS21.m:27 is 0.1/12 = 0.008333, config.py:299 is 0.074830/12 = 0.006236. (d) A FIFTH MISMATCH THE PROPOSAL MISSES: GS21.m:35 sets xi = 0.03/3*3 = 0.03 while config.py:296 sets GS21_ZETA = 0.03/3 = 0.01. The refinancing intensity in the simulation and in sdf_compute_gs21.py:132 is one third of the value the value function was solved under. Because all interpolators are built with fill_value=None (sdf_compute_gs21.py:61-74) the pipeline silently LINEARLY EXTRAPOLATES the value function off-grid for roughly 0.6-0.7% of firm-months -- and linear extrapolation annihilates curvature precisely in the tails, which is the region every nonlinearity proposal (3, 4, 5) wants to activate. Nothing measured today about GS21's tail behaviour is trustworthy. THE ECONOMIC HALF IS COUNTERPRODUCTIVE FOR THE STATED GOAL. The proposal is honest that FM captures 76-92% of a monotone heteroskedasticity channel and that the standalone effect on the DKKM/FM ratio is 1.03 -> 1.05-1.15.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and it likely moves the ratio the wrong way. The diagnosis established that 89-97% of GS21's max squared Sharpe is the 'alpha leg', sd(alpha)/idio_vol * sqrt(N) = 4.33e-4/0.0203 * sqrt(200) = 0.301. Raising sigma_z 10x raises idiosyncratic return volatility roughly proportionally, so that leg's SQUARED Sharpe falls by ~100x and SR* collapses from 0.44/month toward the market leg of 0.035-0.107. The proposal frames this as good ('moves toward the real-data regime'), but it is bad for the DKKM/FM comparison specifically: Sharpe = SR* * cos_Sigma(w, w*), and lowering SR* while leaving the truth 3-dimensional and 79-90% linear in chars raises estimation noise for every method WITHOUT creating bias for the small model to suffer from. That is textbook bias-variance: shrinkage over a rich basis pays only when the small model is BIASED. GS21's small model is not biased, it is nearly correctly specified (R^2(w* | 6 linear chars) = 0.79-0.90). Adding noise in that regime strictly favours the lower-dimensional estimator. The est3.py experiment in the theory diagnosis makes the same point directly: with a linear truth and homogeneous d, OLS-lin(6) = 0.267 BEATS ridge-RFF(3600) = 0.254. Also note the sigma_x repair goes the wrong way for headline Sharpes -- it LOWERS aggregate volatility 1.484x. And the claimed 8.6x range in d log P/d z over the grid is measured in a region (b = 1, x = -4sd) that the state process, per finding (1) above, can never visit because b <= 0.3158.
verdicts.salvage: Ship the reconciliation as a standalone, non-negotiable prerequisite: make config.py and GS21.m agree on sigma_x, sigma_z, rho_z, r and zeta, and add an explicit off-grid counter to create_arrays and integ_zi_zj_x so the 0.6-0.7% extrapolation rate is reported rather than silent. Do NOT sell the sigma_z restoration as a DKKM lever -- sell it as a calibration-realism fix (pairwise correlation 0.95 -> 0.35-0.55) and report every Sharpe as Sharpe/SR* so the collapse in SR* does not read as a failure. If you do restore sigma_z, restore it to the SOLVED value 0.009560 first and re-solve at the paper value second, and check the HJ bound: max_sr must satisfy max_sr <= sqrt(exp(gamma_x^2)-1) = 0.5329/month given GS21.m:28,138. The diagnosis's extrapolated N=1000 figure of 0.62/month VIOLATES that bound by 16%, which is a numerical-conditioning alarm on scipy.linalg.solve(ER, ..., assume_a='pos') at sdf_compute_gs21.py:207 (which, incidentally, uses scipy.linalg without importing it), not an economic result.

verdicts.proposal_name: P4: Five permanent industry types with 5x spread in sigma_z
verdicts.critique: This is a pure D-matrix change and D is diversifiable. The theory diagnosis already ran the decisive experiment (span2.py): under exact K-factor pricing with N=1000, adding d proportional to exp(6*x2) -- a 20x variance spread -- moved the maximum Sharpe from 0.0999 to 0.1000 and the linear-char span from 0.0999 to 0.1000, a RFF/linear ceiling ratio of 0.999. Heteroskedastic D is a multiplier on an unspanned premium and is worth O(1/N) without one. GS21 does have a genuine near-arbitrage alpha leg, so the multiplier is not literally zero: with alpha independent of d and sd(log d) rising 0.25 -> 0.75, E[1/d] rises by exp((0.75^2-0.25^2)/2) = 1.28, so SR_alpha rises ~13%. But that raises SR* for EVERYONE, including FM. The DKKM-specific part is only the nonlinearity of 1/d in char space, and the proposal itself concedes 76-86% linear R^2 for a monotone inverse-variance tilt (its own exp(-c*u) calculation: 0.861 at 25x, 0.763 at 100x). Second problem: PERMANENT types are a fixed effect. Over a 360-month rolling window FM re-estimated monthly with cfvol as a regressor learns the type essentially perfectly, and FF's 2x3 size x cfvol sort captures the monotone part cleanly. The proposal's own risk section identifies this and proposes a slow Markov migration instead -- take that. Third: the whole DKKM edge is claimed to rest on cfvol being a NOISY proxy so the optimal map is a nonlinear shrinkage. But the sampling noise of a 36-month volatility estimate is sigma/sqrt(2*36) = 11.8% of sigma against a 5x cross-sectional spread in sigma, i.e. a signal-to-noise ratio of about 14:1 in logs. At that SNR the optimal shrinkage map is essentially the identity and FM's unpenalized linear regressor on cfvol recovers nearly all of it. To make the shrinkage map genuinely nonlinear you would need the proxy noise comparable to the type dispersion, which means a ~6-month window, which is not defensible.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM gets 76-86% of the tilt by the proposal's own arithmetic, and FF's 2x3 sorts get the monotone part. The proposal's own predicted standalone number is f_lin 0.871 -> 0.75-0.82 of max SR^2 with RFF holding 0.97-0.99, which is DKKM/FM in Sharpe of sqrt(0.988/0.78)/sqrt(0.988/0.932) = 1.09, i.e. +9 percentage points on a target of +200 to +400. The claimed multiplier effect on P1 is void because P1's channel is 90-99.6% linear in raw chars (measured above), so multiplying it by a heteroskedastic D multiplies a linear object -- and D^{-1}*linear is a ratio of two objects both of which FM's raw-level regressors span well. The specific span2.py result the proposal cites (RFF/linear ceiling 1.00 -> 1.91 with a linear alpha plus het D) requires the linear alpha and the het D to be functions of DIFFERENT characteristics with a 100x d range; here both G/P and 1/sigma_z^2 route through leverage and the type, and the range is 25x. FAILURE MODE CHECK: a 25x spread in idiosyncratic variance makes w* = D^{-1}(mu - beta*lambda) put 25x weight on the lowest-vol type. The current cond_var has min eigenvalue 2.391e-4 and cond(ER) = 8.86e5 at N=200, scaling roughly linearly in N; the 0.447x type cuts its idio variance 5x, pushing cond(ER) toward 2e7 at N=1000. scipy.linalg.solve(..., assume_a='pos') at sdf_compute_gs21.py:207 raises no error on a near-singular ER -- this is the documented mechanism behind the 1e9 true SDF weights in the original-vol run. max_sr and both metrics would then be set by a handful of low-variance firms with no information content for any estimator.
verdicts.salvage: Keep the type heterogeneity but move it from D to B. The reason it is inert is that sigma_z changes idiosyncratic variance, which diversifies away; it does not change the firm's exposure to the priced shock, which is what the Sharpe metric rewards. Give the five types different CASH-FLOW DURATION instead -- heterogeneous rho_z, or heterogeneous g and investment-cost scale, or heterogeneous delta -- so that d log P / d x differs across types. That creates genuine cross-sectional dispersion in beta_x (currently essentially nil: the diagnosis measured d log P/d x = 12.4 with the debt channel adding almost nothing, 27.3 at b=0 vs 24.0 at b=1) and it maps to observables (bm, size) through a nonlinear valuation relation rather than a monotone one. If you keep sigma_z heterogeneity, make it a slow Markov migration rather than a permanent type, and verify before running the pipeline that R^2(1/sigma_z,i | rank of cfvol_i, linear) is below 0.85.

verdicts.proposal_name: P5: Turn on kappa_e, raise tau, widen bmax so the equity-issuance kink and the default boundary become reachable
verdicts.critique: The two halves have very different merit and the proposal bundles them. THE kappa_e KINK IS QUANTITATIVELY DEAD AND CANNOT BE REVIVED BY THIS CHANGE. GS21's price-to-flow ratio is P_ex/CF = 190/0.986 = 193 months. The kink perturbs the flow by kappa_e*|prof| only when prof <= 0. Trigger location: prof = (1-tau)exp(x+z) - delta - (1-tau)b = 0 requires x+z = log((delta + (1-tau)b)/(1-tau)) = -1.13 at the current tau = 0.0667 and b* = 0.3158, against sd(x+z) = sqrt(0.05704^2 + 0.05389^2) = 0.0785. That is -14.4 standard deviations: unreachable by a factor that no recalibration of tau or bmax touches. Under the proposal's own tau = 0.20 with b* pushed to 0.5 the threshold moves to x+z = -0.677, still -8.6 sd unless proposal 3's sigma_z restoration is also shipped, at which point it is -1.2 sd and reachable in ~11% of firm-months. But the AMPLITUDE is then still negligible: kappa_e = 0.05 applied to |prof| of order 0.1-0.3 per unit capital is 0.005-0.015 against a price of 100-190, i.e. 0.005-0.015% of value per month, capitalized over the ~50-month state persistence to 0.25-0.75% of value. Against a systematic return volatility of 10-12%/month that is a rounding error. THE DEFAULT HALF IS THE ONE GENUINE MECHANISM IN THE ENTIRE LIST, and I want to say so explicitly. GS21's alpha leg -- 89-97% of max SR^2 -- is precisely the premium on firm-specific CURVATURE of P'(x'), i.e. the components of the return that lie outside the rank-1 top eigenvector of the systematic block. A live default boundary is the only proposed change that materially disperses that curvature, because the equity claim becomes a call option whose convexity in BOTH x' and z' explodes as P -> 0. That is a real economic mechanism aimed at the right object. BUT: I verified that the default region does not exist anywhere on the solved grid (min(P_down.csv) = 4.728, min(P_up.csv) = 10.064 over all 200x20x20 points) and that z_cut_down.csv and z_cut_up.csv each contain exactly one distinct value, -0.146826 = zgrid.min(), at every (x,b) -- the solver found no interior threshold anywhere. Getting from there to a 1%/yr default rate requires the sigma_z restoration, bmax >= 1.5, a joint (bmax, sigma_m) calibration search, and a re-solve, and tauchen.m is not in the repo.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Three reasons the default channel underdelivers even if it works. (a) IT IS MONOTONE. The default-probability effect is convex but strictly monotone in distance-to-default, and the proposal itself computes the linear R^2 of exp(-c*u) at 0.763 for a 100x range. With dd supplied as a char (P2), FM captures 76%+ and DKKM's rank-standardized basis -- which the pipeline audit shows is 49% raw-linear and 87% quadratic in the rank chars -- captures the rest of a smooth convex monotone function almost as easily. The proposal's genuinely correct sub-argument is (a-ii), that a step in the TAIL is much less linear than a step at the median (R^2 0.27 vs 0.75), and that FF value-weights away exactly the distressed left tail. That predicts a large DKKM/FF gap and only a modest DKKM/FM gap -- but FM is the binding benchmark, and the diagnosis already shows FM at 0.932 of max SR^2 versus FF at 0.734. (b) DEFAULT RISK HERE IS NOT PRICED. Default is triggered by z (idiosyncratic) and by the i.i.d. valuation shock nu (GS21.m:53-59, 204, 210, 263), neither of which appears in the SDF (GS21.m:138, Mmat depends on the x innovation only). So default adds idiosyncratic left-tail variance, which RAISES d and LOWERS SR^2 through the alpha leg's 1/d. The convexity channel has to beat that. (c) THE METRIC CANNOT SEE THE TAIL. Sharpe_t = w'rp_t / sqrt(w' Sigma_t w) uses only the first two conditional moments (utils/evaluate_sdfs.py:182-209), so a fat left tail enters ONLY through the variance and is therefore a pure penalty. The real-data 'distressed microcap' channel that DKKM's own decomposition attributes most of their Sharpe to is invisible to this metric by construction. FAILURE MODE CHECK, which is severe here: the sigma_m = 5 valuation shock in GS21.m is an economically real i.i.d. shock to the continuation value (P_up_old_pert = E[max(P'+nu,0)]), not a numerical smoother. If the simulation draws it consistently, as the proposal requires, it injects 5/190 = 2.6%/month of PURE UNPRICED idiosyncratic noise -- LARGER than GS21's current total idiosyncratic volatility of 2.03%/month. That alone would cut SR* by more than half and would have to be added to cond_var or the 'true' moments become wrong. Second failure mode: with real defaults, prices approach zero, returns approach -100%, ER conditioning degrades for real, and panel_functions_gs21.py:73-89 has two latent bugs that only fire once defaults exist (the all-firms-default branch never writes the redrawn xt back into x[t] at line 85, and the while loop has no iteration cap).
verdicts.salvage: Ship the default half only, and only after (i) the parameter reconciliation, (ii) removal of the arbitrary P_ex floor at panel_functions_gs21.py:131, (iii) fixing the two default-replacement bugs, and (iv) a documented decision on sigma_m -- either set it to zero in BOTH the solve and the simulation, or recalibrate it jointly so that the induced 2.6%/month valuation noise does not swamp the economics. Drop kappa_e entirely; it is 0.007%/month of return effect and buys nothing. Then test the mechanism BEFORE running the estimator with the diagnostic that actually predicts the outcome: on the re-solved grid, compute for a simulated cross-section the second-order coefficient c_i2 of P_i(x')/P_i in a Hermite expansion of x', and report R^2(c_i2 | raw linear chars) and R^2(c_i2 | rank-quadratic). GS21's alpha lives in the dispersion of c_i2, and unless that R^2 falls well below 0.5 the default channel will be another monotone-in-dd object that FM eats.

verdicts.proposal_name: P6: An independent credit-conditions state s_t with its own price of risk gamma_s
verdicts.critique: This inherits P1's fatal defect and adds a 64 GB memory wall on top of it. The cross-sectional loading is stipulated to be beta_s,i = (P_up_i - P_down_i)/P_ex,i -- exactly the object I measured off the shipped solution files. It is 89.8% linear in the CURRENT raw chars {size, bm, mkt_lev}, 99.6% linear once book_lev is added, and 94.7%/99.7% linear at the proposal's own kappa_b = 0.02. It is 0.548 in rank-linear and 0.801 in rank-quadratic space, i.e. DKKM's basis represents it WORSE than FM's raw-level basis does. The claim 'FM's X(X'X)^{-1} weights place exactly zero loading on it' is false as a matter of measurement, and false in principle too: the symmetric-function argument requires the characteristic's marginal to be symmetric about the vertex, whereas b_it <= max(b_refin) = 0.3158 by the law of motion at panel_functions_gs21.py:117-119, so the realized support is entirely on one arm. Beyond that, the proposal misstates what a second shock buys. With two priced shocks the economy is still EXACT two-factor: Sigma = B Omega B' + D and mu = B lambda with B = [b_x, b_s]. There is still no alpha -- no component of expected returns that is not proportional to a covariance loading. The theory diagnosis's span2.py established that under exact K-factor pricing with N = 1000, ANY well-diversified portfolio with the correct factor exposure attains SR* to within 0.19%. A second shock changes the dimension of the exposure space from 1 to 2, which a 7-factor FM regression handles trivially when the loadings are 90-99.6% linear in chars. The proposal's condition-(C3) framing is also misapplied: DKKM Theorem 3 is a condition on the effective rank of E[F_t F_t'], which the audit measured at 20.7 for GS21's feature map and which is a property of the FEATURE construction, not of the number of aggregate shocks. Going from 1 to 2 shocks moves EffRank from ~2 to ~3 against an AIPT target in the hundreds.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: It is strictly WEAKER than proposal 1 at roughly 20x the cost, by the proposal's own parameterization. The credit loading is priced at gamma_s = 0.101/month here versus gamma_x = 0.5/month when the same loading is driven by x under proposal 1 -- a factor of 5 less premium for identical cross-sectional shape. Redoing my proposal-1 arithmetic with lambda = 0.101: the new premium component has cross-sectional sd of 4.9e-4 * 0.101 = 5.0e-5 against sd(mu) = 4.0-5.6e-4, i.e. 1.4% of var(mu), of which 0.4-10% is outside FM's span. Incremental unspanned share of SR^2: under 0.15%. The proposal's own stated fallback -- 'alone, expect only ~1.2-1.3x' -- is itself an overestimate by roughly an order of magnitude. On the ceiling: the model's HJ bound rises from sqrt(exp(0.5^2)-1) = 0.5329/month to sqrt(exp(0.25+0.101^2)-1) = 0.5452/month, i.e. +2.2%, so max_sr essentially cannot move. Since Sharpe = SR* * cos_Sigma(w, w*) and SR* is pinned, the entire claimed 2.0-3.0x DKKM/FM ratio would have to come from FM's cosine collapsing by a factor of 2-3, and I measured FM's representation of the one new object at 90-99.6%. Implementation: the proposal is candid that Mmat goes to 400,000 x 20,000 = 64 GB and that the VFI must be rewritten, and tauchen.m is absent from the repo with no MATLAB installed. Spending a multi-week rewrite to add a factor that carries one fifth the price of risk of the shock already in the model, attached to a loading that FM spans linearly, is the worst cost-benefit ratio in the list.
verdicts.salvage: The one thing that would justify a second shock is if it were priced at a magnitude COMPARABLE to gamma_x and attached to a loading that is genuinely nonlinear in observables -- neither of which holds here. If a second state is worth adding, attach it to the INVESTMENT technology rather than to refinancing: a shock to the aggregate investment-cost distribution (imax_t, currently a fixed 2000 with a cutoff of ~40, so the real option is economically dead at P(invest) = 1.98%/month) would move the option value of every firm, and option value is convex in the firm's own state, so the loading is a genuinely nonlinear function of (z, k, b). That routes the second shock through curvature rather than through a monotone leverage index, which is the only place GS21's alpha actually lives. Even then, do the diagnostic first: simulate the cross-section, compute the new loading, and report R^2 on the RAW linear char span before writing any MATLAB.

missed_ideas: THE INVESTMENT OPTION IS THE NATIVE SOURCE OF CHAR-DEPENDENT CURVATURE AND IT IS DEAD. i_cut_down.csv has mean 39.6 against GS21_IMAX = 2000, so P(invest) = 1.98%/month and the real option's exercise region is 2% of the cost support. GS21's alpha leg -- 89-97% of max SR^2 -- is the premium on firm-specific CURVATURE of P'(x'), i.e. the part of mu not proportional to the top eigenvector of the rank-1 systematic block. Convexity in the aggregate state is exactly what a real option delivers, and it is a nonlinear function of (z, b, k) rather than a monotone index. Cutting imax by 20-50x (or making the cost distribution heavy-tailed, or raising g) so the option is a large, state-dependent share of value creates dispersion in the curvature coefficient with NO new shocks, NO new frictions, and only a single re-solve at unchanged grid dimensions. This is the cheapest change in the whole design space that targets the object the metric actually rewards, and none of the six proposals touches it.

NO PROPOSAL CREATES DISPERSION IN beta_x, AND THAT IS THE FIRST-ORDER OMISSION. The diagnosis measured d log P/d x = 27.3 at b = 0 versus 24.0 at b = 1 (x = -4sd) and 7.5 versus 8.5 at x = +4sd -- there is essentially no leverage amplification of the aggregate beta, because debt value is as x-elastic as equity value. Proposals 4 and 3 move D (diversifiable, O(1/N) under exact factor pricing); proposals 1 and 6 move a loading that is 90-99.6% linear. Nobody proposes heterogeneity in CASH-FLOW DURATION -- firm-specific rho_z, delta, g, or investment technology -- which is the only clean way to disperse beta_x. Duration maps to observables (bm, size) through a nonlinear valuation relation, so the resulting beta_x(chars) is genuinely nonlinear, and unlike D-heterogeneity it does not diversify away.

MEASUREMENT ERROR ON THE CHARACTERISTICS, NOT MORE CHARACTERISTICS. bm = 1/P_ex holds exactly (np.allclose verified in the prior diagnosis), mkt_lev = b/P_ex, size = log k + log P_ex, and rank-standardized roe is the exact rank of lagged z. Four chars invert the entire (k, b, z) state with zero error, which is precisely why an MLP recovers 98.3% of the true SDF weight and why GS21 sits in DKKM's APT rather than AIPT regime. Proposal 2 adds MORE exact state information (dd = current z, since z_cut_down.csv is a single constant -0.146826 everywhere). The correct move is the opposite: add i.i.d. multiplicative noise (10-20%) and a 1-3 month reporting lag to bm, roe and book_lev in create_panel. Roughly five lines, no re-solve, no MATLAB. It is the only change that makes the optimal weight a nonlinear SHRINKAGE map of the observables, which unpenalized OLS on 7 factors (config.ALPHA_LST_FAMA = [0]) structurally cannot represent and ridge over a rich basis structurally can.

RECONCILE THE SOLVE AND THE SIMULATION BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE -- THERE ARE FIVE MISMATCHES, NOT FOUR. GS21.m:35 sets xi = 0.03/3*3 = 0.03 while config.py:296 sets GS21_ZETA = 0.03/3 = 0.01: the panel and sdf_compute_gs21.py:132 run at one third of the refinancing intensity the value function was solved with. Only proposal 3 mentions the sigma_x/sigma_z/r mismatches and it misses the zeta one -- which matters most, because it is the exact parameter proposals 1 and 6 want to make stochastic. Also: every interpolator is built with fill_value=None (sdf_compute_gs21.py:61-74), so the pipeline silently LINEARLY EXTRAPOLATES the value function for the ~0.6-0.7% of firm-months outside the solved grid. Linear extrapolation destroys curvature exactly in the tails, which is the region proposals 3, 4 and 5 all want to activate. Add an off-grid counter before trusting any tail measurement.

VALIDATE max_sr AGAINST THE MODEL'S OWN HJ BOUND BEFORE INTERPRETING ANY RESULT. GS21.m:138 sets Mmat = exp(-r - 0.5*gamma_x^2 - gamma_x*eps_x') with gamma_x = 0.5, so the monthly Sharpe of any correctly priced portfolio is bounded by sqrt(exp(0.25)-1) = 0.5329. The measured 0.438 at N=500 is consistent; the extrapolated 0.62 at N=1000 is a 16% VIOLATION and is a conditioning alarm on scipy.linalg.solve(ER, ones, assume_a='pos') at sdf_compute_gs21.py:207 (which also uses scipy.linalg without importing it -- it resolves only by transitive attribute binding). Report max_sr/0.5329 as a gate in every run. Any proposal whose predicted effect is 'max_sr rises' should be treated as a red flag unless it adds a priced shock, because nothing else can raise the bound.

THE FREE ESTIMATOR-SIDE MOVES ARE UNPRICED IN ALL SIX PROPOSALS. NMAT = 5 (config.py; estimate_sdf_dkkm.py:134-169) averages stock weights across 5 independent W draws, which converges to kernel ridge with the same explicit penalty, cancels exactly the draw-specific high-frequency components, and mechanically FLATTENS the Sharpe-vs-nfeatures curve -- the root codebase used nmat = 1. N_DKKM_FEATURES_LIST tops out at 3600 (c = 10) against DKKM's headline c = 1000. The RFF effective rank at L = 6 is 20.7 against DKKM's AIPT target of ~500. All three are config-line changes with no re-solve and no economics, and they bound what ANY model change can deliver: if the estimator can only express ~21 effective dimensions, no amount of structural nonlinearity is reachable. Fix these first so that a null result on a structural change is informative.

GIVE THE PRICING-ERROR TEST SOME POWER. generate_25_portfolios.py sorts only on mve and bm -- two of the six characteristics every method already spans linearly -- so compute_pricing_errors.py's alpha'Sigma^{-1}alpha and GRS cannot detect the nonlinear-in-characteristics content that every one of these proposals claims to create. Add test assets sorted on deciles of the model's TRUE conditional SDF weight, on |mkt_lev - b*(z,x)| (the exact object proposals 1 and 6 claim to create), and on interactions. This costs nothing and is the only metric in the pipeline that is not scale-invariant-per-month (unlike Sharpe, which gives zero credit for conditional timing) and not leverage-contaminated (unlike HJD, whose GS21 FF value of 2.3465 alongside the best Fama Sharpe of 0.4433 is a pure over-leverage artifact).

RUN A CHEAP PRE-COMMITTED SCREEN ON EVERY PROPOSAL BEFORE ANY MATLAB RE-SOLVE. For any proposed new loading or premium component v_i, the maximum achievable DKKM-over-FM Sharpe ratio is bounded by sqrt(f_RFF/f_FM) where f is the fraction of max SR^2 in each span. The single number that predicts it is R^2(v_i | 1, RAW chars) computed on a simulated cross-section with x held common. FM uses raw levels (fama_functions.py:152-165, standardization commented out), so ranks are the wrong space to test in -- and in fact the rank basis DKKM must use is often WORSE than FM's raw basis, as I measured for G/P (0.55 rank-linear, 0.80 rank-quadratic, versus 0.90 raw-linear for FM). Pre-commit to a threshold: unless R^2(v | raw chars) < 0.5, the proposal cannot move the DKKM/FM ratio by more than a few percent. Applying this screen to the six proposals as written would have rejected 1, 2 and 6 in an afternoon without touching MATLAB.

THE TARGET IS ARITHMETICALLY OUT OF REACH FOR ANY LOADING-SHAPE CHANGE, AND THE PROPOSALS SHOULD SAY SO. Today f_lin = 0.871, f_FM = 0.932 and f_RFF360 = 0.988 of max SR^2, giving DKKM/FM = sqrt(0.988/0.932) = 1.030. To reach a 3x ratio you need f_FM = 0.988/9 = 0.110, i.e. 89% of mu'Sigma^{-1}mu must lie OUTSIDE the linear span of the raw characteristics. Since GS21 is a frictionless rational-expectations economy in which mu is by construction minus the covariance with the SDF, no change to the shock structure or to the loading function can create a component of expected returns that is not proportional to a covariance loading. The only ways to get to 0.110 are (a) make the loading function itself a high-frequency, non-monotone function of the observables -- which needs curvature dispersion, not leverage tilts -- or (b) break the exact char->state invertibility with measurement error so that even a linear truth is not linearly recoverable, or (c) introduce a genuine non-risk premium (demand/belief wedge, segmented marginal investor), which changes what 'true' means and should be argued as heterogeneous agents rather than mispricing. None of the six proposals does (a) at scale, and only proposal 2's cfvol gestures at (b) with a variable that measures nothing.
